subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstan: can I save a compiled model?

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstan: can I save a compiled model?
parts:
Hi--how about this example from that page:
---

fit1 <- stan(file = '8schools.stan', data = schools_dat, 
             iter = 1000, chains = 4)
Once a model is fitted, we can use the fitted result as an input to fit the model with other data or settings. This would save us time of compiling the C++ code for the model. By specifying parameter fit for function stan, we can fit the model again. For example, if we want to sample more iterations, we can proceed as follows.

fit2 <- stan(fit = fit1, data = schools_dat, iter = 10000, chains = 4)
---

Yes, you do need data to compile the model that first time, but then when you re-run the compiled model you can feed in new data.  The data you use for compiling the model can be anything---actually, if we really wanted, we could create a "compile-only" mode for Stan where you would supply the model with no data, then Stan could just compile with fake data (e.g., setting all unconstrained parameters to 0, setting positive parameters to 1, setting constrained parameters to the midpoint of their range, etc) and then running for just 1 iteration to give it a chance to catch any gross bugs.  I don't know if that setting would be worth creating or not.  It's one more option (thus making life more complicated) but maybe it would be helpful.  But, in the meantime, you can certainly do this yourself by simply compiling the model and running for 10 iterations with whatever data you want.
AG

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Rstan: can I save a compiled model?
parts:
Yes, you can definitely do that.  That's the "fit = " argument in the stan() call.  The only thing is that in the current implementaiton, you do need to supply data (even if meaningless) for that first, compiling call.  But it doesn't matter what the data are.
A

On Feb 13, 2013, at 11:49 PM, Adam Kiezun wrote:

I see. I was actually using something simpler:

sm <- stan_model(file = 'model.stan')
fit1 <- sampling(sm, data = my.data1, ....)
fit2 <- sampling(sm, data = my.data2, ....)

etc.
the question is then, can I save the 'sm' variable (ie the compiled model) somehow and then load it already compiled next time? (i tried save followed by load, but without luck)
./adam
